2. SMT. SOUMYA A. S.,
 W/O. MANOHAR.

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR REGISTERED IN CR.NO.1/2017 AND ENTIRE PROCEEDINGS PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE VII ADDITIONAL CIVIL JUDGE (Sr.Dn.) AND JMFC MYSURU IN C.C.NO.126/2018 AGAINST THE P/U/S.498-A,504 R/W SEC.34 OF IPC AND SEC.3 AND 4 OF DP ACT.
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.126/2018 (Crime No.1 of 2017) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2.

During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amicably amongst themselves and in this regard have filed a memo reporting settlement NC:
2023:KHC:21539 before this Court.
The parties were also before the Family Court, Mysuru in M.C.No.1009 of 2022 wherein the marriage is dissolved drawing up certain conditions, one such condition is closure of the present proceedings.

The condition insofar as it relates to closure of the present proceedings reads as follows:
"4.
Further, it is stated that the petitioners decided to get their marriage dissolved amicably by decree of divorce by mutual consent under the following terms and conditions.
a. The marriage between the petitioners is irretrievably broken down and there is no chance for them to join together to lead a marital life.

b. The 1st petitioner who has filed a criminal case against the 2nd petitioner in C.C.No.126/2018 under sec.498(A) I.P.C. read with sec 3 and 4 Dowry Prohibition Act on the file of VII Addl. Sr. Civil Judge and CJM, Mysuru, and has undertaken to assist the 2nd petitioner in getting the matter closed.

Prl. Family Court, Mysuru, wherein the 1st petitioner did not press the petition for maintenance for herself but continued the petition for the maintenance of minor daughter which came to be allowed on 08.04.2019 awarding monthly maintenance of Rs.8,000/- from the date of petition till she marries or she gets gainful job.

entities.text: IV Addl. Prl. Family Court, Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The RPFC filed by the 2nd petitioner in RPFC No.91/2019 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka came to be dismissed on merits on 10.12.2020."
NC: 2023:KHC:21539 3.

Since the offences alleged against the petitioners are punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and other offences, which are not against the State or the Society, and in the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties as aforesaid, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) Impugned proceedings in C.C.No.126/2018 pending before the VII Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysore stands quashed qua the petitioners.
